why: Step 254 audited earnings-call transcripts and closed the family unstarted because per-ticker retrieval would take ~87 hours and coverage tracked company size. No return was ever measured. A bulk free source now exists: HuggingFace kurry/sp500_earnings_transcripts (MIT), 33,362 calls of S&P 500 constituents and large caps, 2005-2025, each with a call date. Restricting to large caps is the coverage problem Step 254 named; here it is declared as the universe rather than hidden in it.
dictionary: Loughran-McDonald positive and negative word lists as shipped in pysentiment2 0.1.1 (static/LM.csv, MIT package). The LM lists are free for academic research use; this is research use.

signals.T1_tone: (positive - negative) / (positive + negative) over the full transcript text
signals.T2_tone_change: T1 minus the same company's T1 on its previous call (a tone surprise; each company is compared with itself, which removes industry and style differences in how managers talk)

point_in_time: a call is usable from the weekly close strictly after date + 1 day; the forward window starts at the next weekly close

measurement.decisions: every 4 weeks; the cross-section is each company's most recent call in the prior 13 weeks
measurement.measures: rank IC, decile spread, monotonicity, block bootstrap, both halves
measurement.identity: transcript symbol matched to the price panel through the Yahoo history catalogue's current symbols; match rate reported
